definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese preserved food made by salting and drying ume (Japanese apricot) fruits, often with red shiso leaves for color. Known for their extremely sour and salty taste.

examples.japanese: {梅干|うめぼ}し⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{酸|す}っぱい。
⟦おにぎり→おにぎり：04956_onigiri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{具|ぐ}→具：07857_gu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{梅干|うめぼ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
examples.english: I like umeboshi as a rice ball filling.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{梅干|うめぼ}し is one of the most iconic traditional Japanese preserved foods. It has been a staple of the Japanese diet for centuries and is associated with health benefits, including aiding digestion and preventing fatigue.

⟦{日|ひ}の{丸|まる}→日の丸：19387_hinomaru⟧⟦{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧ (hinomaru bentou) is a simple lunch box with white rice and a single red {梅干|うめぼ}し in the center, resembling the Japanese flag.

The sourness is so well-known that just thinking about {梅干|うめぼ}し can make one's mouth water — a common example in Japanese physiology discussions.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{梅|うめ}→梅：01869_ume⟧ (plum/Japanese apricot) + {干|ほ}し (drying) — literally "dried plum." The し is the conjunctive form of the verb ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧ (to dry).
